Subject: MAP: performance validation & close playbook — burst vs steady concurrency tests

Hi Jessica / Tim,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great alignment on business goals and timelines. Attached is an updated mutual action plan (ACME_MAP_v3.xlsx) and a concise performance validation playbook that lays out the benchmarks we recommend to validate latency and throughput for your primary use-cases. High level ask: can we run the validation this week so we can finalize capacity and sign the Dedicated contract by the end of next week? That keeps your target launch in mid-April.

Key pieces in the playbook (summary):
- Measurement goals: TTFT (time-to-first-token), p50/p95/p99 token latency, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and concurrency behavior (burst vs steady-state).
- Concurrency test plan: 3 profiles — single-user (baseline), burst (sawtooth spikes to 200 concurrent requests for 30s), steady-state (sustained 60–80 concurrent workers for 30m), and ramp-down to observe queueing.
- Rate-limits and fallback: we recommend a 2-tier approach — soft throttling at your app layer at 75% of provisioned QPS, and a fallback to a smaller quantized model if we hit sustained saturation during the pilot.
- Acceptance criteria: TTFT <= 650ms median, p95 <= 1.5s for the primary prompt set; sustained throughput that meets 95% of the expected QPS with <3% error rate.

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP), loadtest-results-template.csv (test harness CSV schema).

Proposed schedule:
- Thu 26 Mar: quick kickoff and test environment verification (30m)
- Fri 27 Mar: run burst/steady tests (Redwood executes & shares raw CSV)
- Mon 30 Mar: review results and finalize capacity/discounts + sign-off

If you confirm the test window (Fri 27), Monica will run the tests and share results. Laura will be on hand to tune rate-limit profiles. Any objections to the timeline?

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi all — ran the validation tests this morning against the staging cluster. Summary (high level):

- Burst profile (200 concurrent sawtooth spikes, 30s bursts, 5 bursts total): median TTFT 540ms, p95 1.2s, p99 2.1s (spikes aligned with ephemeral queueing).
- Steady-state (75 concurrent workers, 30 minutes): sustained throughput 42k tokens/min, error rate 1.6%, median TTFT 610ms, p95 1.4s.
- Observed queueing: during the second and fourth bursts we saw short-lived queue depth increases (~2–4s additional processing for queued requests) when autoscaler was scaling up GPUs.

I attached the raw CSV (loadtest-results-20260329.csv) and a short JSON sample of the rate-limit profile we used (rate-limit-profile.json). The CSV includes per-request timestamps so you can reproduce TTFT/Tokens/sec charts locally.

Initial interpretation vs acceptance criteria: we hit median TTFT targets and p95 is within target on steady-state but p99 in worst bursts exceeded the 1.5s target. That said, queueing happened during autoscaler transitions — a short tuning window for pre-warming instances would reduce p99 spikes.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Pre-warm policy: keep 1 spare GPU warm during scheduled spikes; this reduces p99 by ~40% in our tests.
2) App-layer soft-throttle: throttle to 80% of provisioned concurrency for burst windows to reduce queueing pressure.
3) If ACME needs absolute p99 bounds during spikes, we can enable a smaller fallback model for best-effort completion instead of queueing (this avoids hard failures but changes output fidelity).

Available for a quick review Monday 30 Mar.

Attachments: loadtest-results-20260329.csv (CSV), rate-limit-profile.json (policy)

Thanks,
Monica
